chapter: Records, Lovie Austin and a first marriage
title: "Chirping the Blues", Glover Compton, Fletcher Henderson, Tony Jackson
summary: Her own "Chirping the Blues" was first recorded unissued with pianist Glover Compton, then reissued with Henderson and was her biggest after Downhearted, under bad contracts. Early in the twenties in Chicago she worked with Tony Jackson, who wrote "Pretty Baby".

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Those three you did with the Original Memphis Five. But now, I notice that 'Chirping the Blues' --
That's mine.
-- that's yours, and the first time you recorded that, it was never issued. So Paramount -- you were accompanied by a pianist named J. Glover Compton.
Yes. You know who Glover Compton was?
No.

You know when I told you about Bricktop and Mattie Hite and all of them working in the Panama? Well, that's another thing I wrote down for you. Glover Compton was a pianist. And he was the husband of Nettie Compton that was there with Bricktop and them in the Panama.
I see. Huh.
Yes, Glover Compton, he later went to Paris, went to Europe.
Oh, he did?
Uh-huh.

And you did that with him, but it was never issued. Then you did 'Chirping the Blues' again the next year, exactly a year later almost. No, you did it just a couple of months later with Fletcher Henderson, and that was the one that came out.
That came out, uh-huh.
Now, that was the -- you said that was very popular, 'Chirping the Blues'?
It was next to Downhearted,' made a lot of money, because I had those old bogus contracts on it, you see. I had those bad contracts.
And you did 'Someone Else Will Take Your Place,' Ramping Brown, and 'You Can Have My Man If He Comes To See You Too.'
Yeah, uh-huh. Yeah, who was that with there?
That was Fletcher on piano. That was Fletcher.
Well, what is this? What --
This is a list of all the records you've made. This -- it's called a discography. Now, tell me something.
Excuse me, but did I tell you that I worked with Tony Jackson, a fellow that wrote 'Pretty Baby'?
No, you didn't tell me that.
I did, in Chicago.
Oh, you did?
Yeah, at the Elkin Number Two.
And this was before you came to New York the first time?
Yeah.
So this was in --
In the '20's.
The '20's, the early -- very early '20's.
Yeah, Tony Jackson.
